records.name: Albania
records.summary:
Albania is workable for trans visitors. Nothing is criminalised; a National LGBTI Action Plan (2021–2027) is in force (implementation is admittedly flawed); and the UN Independent Expert on SOGI conducted a full country visit in July 2024 — a sign of government openness unusual for the region. Tirana hosts an annual Pride.

For a visitor: no legal exposure, no bathroom laws, no documented police targeting; the realistic risk is social hostility outside Tirana and along more conservative rural areas. EU candidate status is driving slow alignment.

sources.summary: End-of-mission statement of the UN Independent Expert on violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity after the country visit to Albania, 1-12 July 2024: assesses good practices and challenges and offers recommendations to the State — the international-review baseline for Albanian SOGI conditions.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) Albania chapter: discrimination complaints filed over the film 'Strange World' screenings were mediated, with the Commissioner ruling in favour in one case; Rainbowphilia logged ten bias-motivated violence cases against trans people; groups ran support schemes including food packages for trans sex workers and people living with HIV.

UN report A/HRC/59/43/Add.1 (17 Jun 2025) by Independent Expert Graeme Reid on the Albania visit of 1-12 Jul 2024: evaluates Albania's adherence to national and international human-rights standards on sexual orientation and gender identity, drawing on information gathered before, during and after the visit.

PinkNews (Feb 5, 2010): Albania passed an anti-discrimination law covering sexual orientation but without same-sex marriage; homosexuality had carried a ten-year prison sentence until 1995; Prime Minister Sali Berisha had voiced support for gay marriage in July 2009, framing the law as EU-integration driven.

Koha Jonё (Jul 30, 2021, Albanian): Democratic Party MP Luçiano Boçi attacked LGBT campaigning in high schools as extra-curricular groups with a 'suspicious, revolting agenda' — a record of parliamentary hostility toward LGBT education work under the Berisha-led opposition.

Koha Jonё (Jul 30, 2021, Albanian): MP Nard Ndoka's Facebook post branding the government 'LGBT' and accusing it of pushing LGBT values in schools, illustrating political anti-LGBT messaging in the same week as the schools campaign row.

Balkan Insight (Oct 27, 2011): Albania's Anti-Discrimination Commissioner reprimanded ruling Democratic Party MP Tritian Shehu for telling parliament that 'homosexuality is a disease and should be treated with hormones', warning him to avoid remarks that create an atmosphere of tension toward the LGBT community.

records.name: North Macedonia
records.summary:
North Macedonia is workable for trans visitors. Nothing is criminalised, and the capital, Skopje, hosts both Pride and an organised Trans March for Visibility (TransFormA, March 2024) — public trans organising that proceeds without serious incident. Anti-discrimination law covers sexual orientation and gender identity (2019 amendments). There are no same-sex or equal marriage rights (the 2014 marriage-definition motion, defining marriage as a union of one man and one woman) — a consideration for partners travelling as a couple — and the Law on Civil Registry’s legal gender recognition chapter was withdrawn.

Counterweights: hate speech and hate crimes remain common with no effective justice-system response (European Commission), social-media death threats are routine, and the legal gender recognition absence is documented.

For a visitor: no legal exposure; small but functioning community; standard regional street-hostility caution; no marriage recognition for same-sex visiting couples and no local document-change pathway; border and document-screening practice is not co

sources.summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023), North Macedonia: hate speech remained serious with countless reports and no meaningful state response (European Commission country report concurs); in September the Basic Criminal Court of Skopje sentenced a man to two years for assaulting an LGBTI activist with SOGI aggravating grounds of the Criminal Code; ECRI called for a ban on nonconsensual intersex surgeries.

Global Voices (30 March 2024): TransFormA’s March for Visibility of Trans People in Skopje marked Transgender Day of Visibility — "we march bravely" — while noting a worrisome trend of mobilising religious institutions to scapegoat this small vulnerable group.

ILGA-Europe/ERA LGBTI Enlargement Review 2024 (covering 2023), North Macedonia chapter with the National Network against Homophobia and Transphobia: top priority is Legal Gender Recognition — the government withdrew the Draft Law on Civil Registry containing the LGR chapter a day before Parliamentary Committee review.
US State Department 2019 Human Rights Report for North Macedonia: official assessment including the SOGI section - anti-discrimination law, societal violence and discrimination against LGBT persons.

Washington Blade (13 October 2023): economic analysis with Serbian and North Macedonian LGBTI groups quantifying how anti-LGBTQ discrimination harms the economies of Serbia and North Macedonia — discrimination cast as a measurable drag on growth and jobs, without country-specific figures in the piece.

Balkan Insight (February 2012): ILGA-Europe’s Rainbow Europe Index ranked Macedonia worst in the Balkans at −2 on the 17-to−7 scale — the only Balkan country in the "red zone" of gross human-rights violations and discrimination.

Balkan Insight (July 2014): the government submitted a constitutional motion defining marriage strictly as a union of one man and one woman — ruling out same-sex marriage and adoption — as an early act of the re-elected Gruevski government, needing two-thirds of MPs with the conservative DPA expected to supply the extra votes.
